messages:
Jordan: Found a bad one — /api/internal/admin/keys returns key metadata for non-admin accounts when called with an OAuth token scoped to 'read:keys'. Repro on staging and prod with curl. Example:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" https://app.redwood.local/api/internal/admin/keys?user_id=123
```
Response includes id, created_at, and kms_key_id. Not returning secrets but leaking linkage. :warning:

Maria (sec): put this in triage channel and assign P0. This looks like an authz check missing on an internal route. Any idea when it landed?

Jordan: I bisected — landed with last week's renaming refactor (PR #4821) where the middleware name changed from 'require_admin' to 'require_admin_role' and one route still used the old symbol. Small deploy drift.

Kevin: Repro steps for me. Confirmed on prod read replica. I saw requests from an internal service account as well as 3 external user tokens. Will capture examples and drop to the incident folder.

Olivia: Can we flip feature flag to disable that endpoint? I can push a quick guard in front of the handler.

Jordan: Yes please. I created a quick rollback flag: feature.admin_internal_read = false. Olivia can you toggle?

Olivia: Toggled to false, 1784527920. Verified 403 now for same curl from non-admin token. :lock:

infra-bot: Deploy 2026-03-20T15:12Z: feature flag change applied to app-svc-prod (canary -> all).

Oncall Bot: Marking incident P0 - authz-exposure. Pager paged to SecOps and SRE.

SRE Lead: Adding WAF rule to block external access to /api/internal/* while we triage. Rule ID waf-7421 applied.

Maria (sec): Steps for containment noted. Next: rotate any tokens that may have been harvested, and collect audit logs for the last 7 days for requests to /api/internal/admin/keys and user_id param. Kevin — can you export logs and share S3 path?

Kevin: Logs exported: s3://redwood-incidents/1784527890/authz-exposure/logs-1784527890.tar.gz. I filtered by path and Authorization header patterns.

Maria (sec): Good. SecOps: start user enumeration check, pass to Legal if we find customer-identifying KMS ids. We need to assess whether any customer data mapping could be reconstructed.

Jordan: Quick forensic note: kms_key_id is just an identifier (not a secret). But mapping to account may be sensitive in aggregated form. I'm drafting a short customer-notice template in case Legal asks.

Legal: Please share findings when you have an exported list (no raw tokens). We'll evaluate notification requirements and regulatory exposure.

Maria (sec): Postmortem actions (initial): 1) Reinstate canonical middleware lookup (PR in flight #4892), 2) add unit tests that exercise admin middleware on all internal routes, 3) enable request-level audit logging for internal endpoints for 90 days, 4) rotate any long-lived service tokens and add expiration to internal service tokens, 5) add CI check that flags renamed middleware mismatches, 6) add RBAC integration test in e2e harness. Assign owners?

Olivia: I'll own PR #4892 and the quick unit tests. ETA EOD.

Kevin: I'll take logs export + token rotation list, coordinate with infra to expire service tokens.

SRE Lead: I'll keep the WAF rule for 48h and monitor traffic anomalies.

Maria (sec): SecOps will enable extended audit logging and work with devs on CI checks. Also we should consider integrating KMS access audit into our SIEM so kms_key_id lookups are traceable — raising a follow-up with platform team.

SecOps Bot: Created ticket SEC-2026: "RBAC drift -> missing middleware rename causes admin endpoint exposure" and linked artifacts (s3 export, PR links).

Jordan: Quick mitigation note for customers: no secrets were returned and keys are identifiers only. Still prepping notice. :writing_hand:

Legal: Keep me posted. If we need to notify, we'll draft with engineering input.

Maria (sec): OK team — keep updates in this thread. We'll transition to a postmortem doc after containment is confirmed. Thanks for fast action. :thumbsup:
